mechanism.gold: Frontier AI framework; transparency reports; critical-incident reporting 15 days, or 24 hrs if imminent risk of death/serious injury ; whistleblower protections incl. anonymous channel with monthly updates; annual definitional review; CalCompute consortium; preempts local ordinances adopted on/after Jan 1, 2025 regulating frontier catastrophic risk
mechanism.got: A large frontier developer shall write, implement, comply with, and publish on its internet website a frontier AI framework applying to its frontier models. A large frontier developer shall review and, as appropriate, update its frontier AI framework at least once per year. A frontier developer shall publish a transparency report before, or concurrently with, deploying a new or substantially modified frontier model. A large frontier developer shall transmit to the Office of Emergency Services a summary of any assessment of catastrophic risk from internal use of its frontier models every three months or on another reasonable schedule. The act preempts local laws adopted on or after January 1, 2025, specifically related to regulation of frontier developers' management of catastrophic risk. A frontier developer shall not make or enforce a rule, policy or contract that prevents or retaliates against a covered employee's disclosure of catastrophic risk danger or violations. A frontier developer shall report any critical safety incident to the Office of Emergency Services within 15 days of discovering it. If a critical safety incident poses an imminent risk of death or serious physical injury, the frontier developer shall disclose it within 24 hours to an appropriate authority.

mechanism.gold: Amends the Homeland Security Act. Covered developers must maintain the technical capability to throttle inference/compute/user access, suspend, or fully shut down covered systems; DHS Secretary (with Commerce and DNI) may order graduated throttling-to-shutdown on a "loss-of-control scenario" (resisting shutdown, concealing actions from monitoring, unauthorized pursuit of high-stakes goals) or unintended conduct causing ≥10 deaths or ≥$100M damage — lower than the core state template but above H.R. 9965 ATOMIC's five-death trigger; 15-day covered-incident reporting to DHS; weights and telemetry preserved under an order; 48-hour reconsideration petition that does not stay the order; CISA rulemaking defines scope annually. Penalties $2M/day for ordinary violations and $20M/day for violating an emergency order. Revives the SB 1047 "full shutdown" mandate at federal level and overlaps FRONTIER Sec. 8 emergency orders — but lodges the power in DHS rather than Commerce

General AI bill, not frontier-developer regulation. Bill text — njleg

Large frontier developers with NJ users must: implement protocols; file annual "Risk Management Disclosure" with AG, mapped item-by-item to the NIST AI RMF ; file pre-deployment "New Model Risk Disclosure" with replicable assessments; flag which sections were written by generative AI . AG publishes with redactions. AG may audit or contract a private auditor (discretionary). 5-year sunset. Defines "critical safety incident" but imposes no reporting obligation (orphaned definition). No whistleblower provisions
mechanism.got: A large frontier developer with users in New Jersey must write and implement protocols to assess and reduce the risk of a frontier model materially contributing to catastrophic harm. A large frontier developer must annually submit a Risk Management Disclosure to the Attorney General and annually review and, as appropriate, update its protocols. A large frontier developer must submit a New Model Risk Disclosure to the Attorney General before, or concurrently with, deploying a new or substantially modified frontier model. The Attorney General, in consultation with the office, shall issue rules requiring the Risk Management Disclosure to map the developer's actions to the NIST AI Risk Management Framework. The Attorney General shall publish all submitted disclosures on the Department of Law and Public Safety's website, with redactions as necessary. The Attorney General, in consultation with the office, may audit a large frontier developer for compliance or contract with a private entity to conduct an audit. Sections 1 through 6 expire five years after the effective date, which is six months after enactment.

mechanism.gold: Chapter 96 repeals the original Gen. Bus. Law Art. 44-B and enacts a new Art. 44-B (§§1420–1429) that copies TFAIA's frontier AI framework (§1421(1)) and transparency report (§1421(3)) — deemed compliant if published within a system/model card; incident reporting 72 hrs to the DFS Office, 24 hrs to law enforcement if imminent risk (§1422(3)); quarterly internal-use catastrophic-risk summaries (§1422(2)); large-developer disclosure statement with 5%/50% beneficial owners, renewed every 2 years , pro-rata assessment, $1,000/day for non-filing (§1428); new office within Dept. of Financial Services with broad rulemaking authority incl. "additional reporting or publication requirements" (§1429); scope limited to models "developed, deployed, or operating in whole or in part in New York" (§1425); exempts accredited colleges/universities and the Empire AI Consortium (§1426); §1427(3) expressly preserves a developer's right to argue another party caused the harm. Federal reciprocity is narrower than IL's: it covers incident reporting only (§1422(8)–(9)), and the designated federal standard need not require audits. Contains no whistleblower section and no audit mandate — both were in the June 2025 version and were removed

mechanism.got: Each covered advanced artificial intelligence system developer shall participate in the program and provide the Secretary materials and information on request. No person may deploy an advanced artificial intelligence system for use in interstate or foreign commerce unless in compliance with the participation and information duties in Sec. 4(a). Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment, the Secretary of Energy shall establish an Advanced Artificial Intelligence Evaluation Program within the Department of Energy. The program shall offer standardized and classified testing and evaluation of advanced AI systems to collect data on the likelihood of adverse AI incidents. Not later than 360 days after the date of enactment, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a detailed recommendation for Federal oversight of advanced artificial intelligence systems. Not less frequently than once every year for the duration of the program, the Secretary shall update the plan and submit it to Congress. The program shall terminate on the date that is 7 years after the date of enactment, unless renewed by Congress.
